 Iasmin Lucindo | Back In The Game
 Promising Strawweight Talent Set To Make Her UFC 333 Return After More Than A Year Outside The Octagon 
 By Steve Latrell
 • Oct. 21, 2026
 By her own admission, Iasmin Lucindo would never be mistaken for a gamer, but when she was finally added to the UFC game from EA Sports , she couldn’t resist giving it a try.
 “I'm not a big fan of video games, but I bought a gaming console to play, and I was very excited. I said, ‘My God, I'm in the game!’” Lucindo said.
 MORE UFC 333: Fight By Fight Preview | Fighters On The Rise | Movsar Evloev: It’s A Long Way To The Top | Alexander Volkanovski: Adversity Above Achievements | Asaf Chopurov: The 'Honey Badger' Is Here | By The Numbers: Movsar Evloev | Merab Dvalishvili: Return of The Machine | Petr Yan Is Chasing A Title Fight Hat-Trick In Abu Dhabi 
 Sitting with UFC.com in Abu Dhabi ahead of her Saturday bout vs Nicolle Caliari, her face lit up when she recalled playing as herself for the first time.
 Iasmin Lucindo of Brazil kicks Karolina Kowalkiewicz of Poland in a strawweight bout during the UFC 301 event at Farmasi Arena on May 04, 2024 in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil (Photo by Alexandre Loureiro/Zuffa LLC)
 “It was pretty surreal to see myself in the game and how closely it resembles me,” she said. “Like even the scar in my eye is the same thing, all the details are there. It's a really surreal experience.”
 That was just one in a long string of unusual experiences for the strawweight that punctuated the past 14 months. It began with a pratfall that all too many mixed martial artists encounter: a tainted supplement which resulted in a positive test and a suspension that kept her out of the Octagon. Even when the suspension was lifted last June, finding a fight proved to be easier said than done.
 WATCH: UFC 333 Embedded 
 “Yeah, it was tough,” she admits. “I've never spent a whole year without competing since I started fighting, so that's a very different experience.”
 Iasmin Lucindo of Brazil punches Angela Hill in a strawweight fight during the UFC Fight Night event at UFC APEX on August 09, 2025 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC)
 It’s worth remembering here that Lucindo has been fighting professionally since the tender age of 15. For nearly the first time in a decade, she was in uncharted waters.
 “It took a lot of mental preparation, finding new habits, getting the idea in my head that I'm not going to be fighting,” she said.
 Watch All The Action Saturday On Paramount+ | How To Watch In Your Country 
 But as she watched her teammates and future opponents continue their journeys, she realized she had to continue hers, even if she didn’t know what the future held.
 “Everybody else is training, everybody is improving, so I have to keep working,” she said. “Even if I don't have a fight. That was the big thing: just staying focused on the fact that I have to keep up with everybody else for whenever I do get to come back.
 Iasmin Lucindo of Brazil poses on the scale during the UFC 307 ceremonial weigh-in at Salt Palace Convention Center on October 04, 2024 in Salt Lake City, Utah (Photo by Cooper Neill/Zuffa LLC)
 “Something that I've always said: whenever you see me competing, you're going to see a different version of me, and this time, even more. I've never had a year to work on my game like this, and you're going to see a very different and improved version of Iasmin.”
 MMA Coach Breaks Down The Bantamweight Yan vs Dvalishvili 3 
 We’ll all get to witness that new Iasmin October 24, when she’ll open the show with fellow Brazilian Caliari at UFC 333. Caliari had a bumpy start under the UFC banner but enters Saturday after her first win in the promotion, a dramatic third-round arm triangle over Shauna Bannon last May. Lucindo expects her opponent to be riding high on that confidence.
 “She's a very explosive fighter, she's very well-rounded, a very good athlete, so I know that it's for sure going to be a great fight,” Lucindo said. “No matter what happens, we're going to deliver a great fight for the fans.”
 A fan-friendly fight, yes, but one that she fully expects to win.
 Iasmin Lucindo of Brazil reacts after her victory against Karolina Kowalkiewicz of Poland in a strawweight bout during the UFC 301 event at Farmasi Arena on May 04, 2024 in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil (Photo by Alexandre Loureiro/Zuffa LLC)
 “The thing is, I believe that I am a complete fighter,” she said. “I'm not afraid of grappling with anyone or striking with anyone. So, I've got to feel the flow of the fight, see where it goes. But overall, my main goal is always to get a finish, no matter where the fight takes place.”

 Saturday will mark the first time in a long time Lucindo will face an opponent without a number next to her name. Lucindo’s time away has dropped her from the rankings as well, a place where she had been a mainstay for years after defeating high-caliber talent like Angela Hill, Marina Rodriguez, Polyana Viana and former title challenger Karolina Kowalkiewicz. For her part, Lucindo seems unconcerned. She is, after all, only 24 years old with 24 professional fights already under her belt.
 “I've done it once; I can do two, three, four, as many times as I need,” she says matter-of-factly. “Up there, I just need to be Iasmin, express myself, and unleash my game.”

This event starts at a special time: Early Prelims begin at 10am ET/7am PT, followed by the Prelims at 12pm ET/9am PT and Main Card at 2pm ET/11am PT, live on Paramount+ in the United States.
